title: ECN 4199 - Industrial Data Analytics
text:
Welcome to the course website for ECN 4199: Industrial Data Analytics.
This course introduces students to:

Python programming
data analytics
data visualisation
machine learning
forecasting
AI tools for economics and business
interactive dashboards
text analytics

The course is designed for students with little or no prior programming experience.
You are not expected to become a computer scientist.
You are expected to become an economist who can work effectively with modern data tools.

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Welcome to ECN 4199 — Industrial Data Analytics.
This week is not about advanced coding. It is about removing fear, understanding the course workflow, and running your first Python code.

title: Week 1: Welcome to AI and Data Analytics for Economics
text:
Example
Suppose we have data on inflation in Sri Lanka.
A basic economist may ask:

Has inflation increased?

A data analyst asks:

By how much did inflation increase?
When did it increase most?
Is the increase temporary or persistent?
Can we forecast next month’s inflation?
How should we communicate this clearly?

That is the mindset of this course.

title: Week 1: Welcome to AI and Data Analytics for Economics
text:
Important message to students
You do not need to memorise Python.
You need to learn how to use it.
Coding is like learning a language. You improve by practising.

title: Week 1: Welcome to AI and Data Analytics for Economics
text:
Economics example
An AI tool can help summarise a central bank report.
But it may also make mistakes.
Therefore, economists must use AI critically.
AI can assist your thinking.
It should not replace your thinking.

title: Week 1: Welcome to AI and Data Analytics for Economics
text:
Example
Suppose we have data on households.
The data includes:

income

A machine learning model may learn patterns that help predict whether a household is likely to be poor.

Machine learning is mainly about prediction.
Economics is often about explanation and causality.
This difference matters.
